newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sapporo Breweries to expand Chinese hop production.
newsitem.headline: Sapporo Breweries to expand Chinese hop production.

text.p: Sapporo Breweries Ltd said on Wednesday that it had decided on several expansion plans for its hop production in China, including investing 1.2 billion yen to build new processing facilities by 2000.
Sapporo, Japan's third largest beer maker, also said it plans to boost aroma hop production to 600 tonnes in 1998, which is almost double the production level expected in 1996.
Sapporo operates with local companies through a joint venture, Xinjiang Fubei Sapporo Hop Corp, the only aroma hop producer in China.

The joint venture firm has been exporting all of its harvest to Sapporo factories in Japan. By 1998, the firm is expected to be shipping 200 tonnes of aroma hops annually to the Chinese market, a Sapporo spokesman said.

The joint venture expects to agree with eight Chinese breweries by the end of this year to supply a total of 30 tonnes of aroma hops, the spokesman said. Sapporo also set up another joint venture, Xinjiang East-Asia Hop Union Corp, in May to produce bitter hops, which are less expensive than aroma hops.
Sapporo aims to raise sales from hop operations in China eleven-fold to 2.5 billion yen by 2000, the spokesman said.
In recent years Japanese beer makers have been rushing to tap the Chinese market, now the world's second largest.
Kirin Brewery Co, Japan's largest beer maker, has licensed 15 factories in China to produce its beer since May 1995.
Sapporo also plans to launch a joint venture with Marubeni Corp and two Chinese beer makers to start producing Sapporo beer in China next year, the company spokesman said.
